problems.quote: This derivation shows that the work done by the net force on a particle equals the change in its kinetic energy, regardless of whether the force is constant or variable, provided the work is evaluated
problems.problem: The derivation shown uses v_f² = v_i² + 2 a s, which assumes constant acceleration (constant force). It does not prove the work-energy theorem for variable forces; the general proof requires integration.
problems.correction: This derivation shows the work-energy theorem for a constant force; the theorem holds generally for variable forces when work is evaluated as the integral of the net force.
problems.verifierReason: Original quote incorrectly claims derivation proves theorem for variable forces; correction accurately limits to constant force and notes general case requires integration.

problems.quote: "She will either call or email" omits the object after email (which can be a verb), creating a shift in parts of speech
problems.problem: The analysis is linguistically incorrect: in "She will either call or email", both "call" and "email" are bare infinitives (verbs), so the structure is parallel; there is no omitted object or part-of-speech shift.
problems.correction: "She will either call or email" is parallel (both verbs); a faulty version would mix forms like "call or send an email".
problems.verifierReason: Original analysis misidentifies parallel verbs as POS shift; correction correctly explains parallel bare infinitives.

problems.quote: always 1

problems.verifierReason: Original formula gives KE, but work done is λLv² (twice KE) due to inelastic pickup. Correction is correct.
